results.title: Three SGX underdog stocks raise dividends amid soft profit trends
results.body: The article discusses three Singapore Exchange‑listed companies that increased their total dividend payouts for the most recent financial year. Credit Bureau Asia lifted its full‑year dividend to S$0,042 per share on a FY2025 revenue of S$60.1 million, profit of S$10.7 million and free cash flow of S$27.2 million, while holding S$71.1 million in liquid assets and no borrowings. Valuetronics announced a FY2026 dividend of HK$0.38 per share, a 41 % rise, backed by free cash flow of HK$178.4 million, cash of HK$1.21 billion and a plan to return HK$300 million to shareholders through special dividends and buybacks, despite a net profit drop to HK$111.4 million. Old Chang Kee raised its total payout to S$0.03 per share, of which S$0.02 is recurring, on FY2026 revenue of S$103.5 million, net profit of S$9.6 million and free cash flow of S$21.0 million, with S$61.6 million cash and minimal debt. The piece notes that each company’s higher dividend is supported by strong cash generation and balance‑sheet strength rather than rising earnings, a point retirees should consider when evaluating sustainable income.
